newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-WESTWOOD IN RECORD-BREAKING FORM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WESTWOOD IN RECORD-BREAKING FORM.

text.p: British prospect Lee Westwood sustained his fine form with a course record six-under-par 65 in the first round of the Irish Open on Thursday.
Westwood's effort, which put him three shots ahead of a class field, beat by one the previous best round at Druid's Glen set by Australian Wayne Riley last year.
Briton David Gilford filled second place, with three times winner Nick Faldo a further stroke back on 69.
A blistering starting burst enabled Westwood's to pick up five strokes over his first five holes -- and prompted praise from Faldo.

"He's a very long driver, 30 yards longer than me," said Faldo, "and that's a plus on a difficult course like this one. Once he learns to win a bit he's going to become quite a dominant force. He'll be an asset to the Ryder Cup team at Valderrama because it can play long there."

Westwood, labelled the European Tour's best youngster by reigning Europen number one Colin Montgomerie last week, was bidding for a second victory after a second and two third places this season. He won the non-Tour Malaysian Open earlier in the year.
"It is a tough course and obviously I benefited from a great start," said Westwood. "It's difficult to make a mess after being five-under after five.
"It's nice that senior pros are saying good things about me but it doesn't put me under pressure. I gain confidence from it.

"I could have won three times this year but each time a great player played just that bit better -- Olazabal, Langer and Montgomerie -- so I know something could happen for me. I just want to keep in contention and hopefully something will fall into place."
Jose Maria Olazabal carded 74 and Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros 75.
